domains.name: Red & Blue Team
domains.tagline: Two perspectives, one discipline — attack to understand, defend to protect. Every exercise is conducted in controlled labs with documented ethical boundaries.
domains.overview: The Red & Blue Team domain bridges adversarial attack simulations with institutional defense. Members practice both offensive penetration testing techniques to uncover attack vectors and defensive operational telemetry to isolate intrusions, engineer detection rules, and execute incident response drills.
focusAreas: Ethical hacking basics & scoped rules of engagement

subTracks.name: Red Team (Offensive Practice)
subTracks.description: Thinking from the attacker position — finding architectural and implementation weaknesses before threat actors exploit them.

subTracks.name: Blue Team (Defensive Operations)
subTracks.description: Watching, detecting, responding — building the organizational muscle that shields mission-critical systems.

learningPathway.title: Foundational Reconnaissance & Lab Setup
learningPathway.description: Establish isolated Kali Linux & target VMs. Master Nmap, port scanning, basic HTTP inspection, and packet flows.
learningPathway.deliverable: Complete basic TryHackMe / HackTheBox pre-security rooms and write a reproducible lab verification memo.

learningPathway.title: Web Application Pentesting & Perimeter Defense
learningPathway.description: Analyze SQL injection, cross-site scripting (XSS), authentication bypasses, and configure Suricata IDS rules.
learningPathway.deliverable: Publish a scoped penetration test report and matching Sigma defensive detection rules for an internal vulnerable service.

learningPathway.title: Full Attack-Defence Simulation & Active Directory
learningPathway.description: Participate in live team vs team scenarios, Kerberoasting, golden ticket attacks, and automated endpoint triage.
learningPathway.deliverable: Lead an internal 0XNULL CTF attack-defence session with automated post-incident debrief.

domains.name: Digital Forensics
domains.tagline: Reconstructing events from artefacts — disk, memory and network traces. The discipline of answering 'what happened' with evidence, not assumption.
domains.overview: Digital Forensics provides the rigorous methodology required to examine compromised storage media, memory dumps, and protocol traces. Members learn chain of custody protocols, volatile memory analysis, and filesystem timelines to piece together digital crime scenes.
focusAreas: Digital evidence handling & legal chain of custody
Disk forensics & RAW / E01 filesystem image carving
Network forensics & deep protocol trace inspection

toolsCovered.name: Wireshark
toolsCovered.description: Packet capture and network traffic protocol analysis to trace malicious C2 communications and payload exfiltration.

toolsCovered.name: Autopsy
toolsCovered.description: Disk, raw image, and filesystem investigation platform for automated artefact indexing, deleted file carving, and timeline analysis.

toolsCovered.name: Volatility
toolsCovered.description: Volatile memory artefact extraction and malware analysis framework for analyzing process trees, injected DLLs, and memory pools.

learningPathway.title: Artefact Acquisition & Hex Analysis
learningPathway.description: Learn evidence hashing (SHA-256), write-blockers, disk cloning, and hex examination of common file signatures.
learningPathway.deliverable: Verify and document a cryptographic disk image integrity verification report.

learningPathway.title: Network & Memory Incident Extraction
learningPathway.description: Dissect PCAP files for credentials, DNS tunneling, and inspect memory dumps using Volatility 3 to spot hidden threads.
learningPathway.deliverable: Deliver an incident timeline report detailing a simulated employee data-exfiltration breach.

learningPathway.title: Enterprise Incident Response & Anti-Forensics
learningPathway.description: Counter timestomping, rootkits, memory injection, and reconstruct lateral movement across Windows event logs.
learningPathway.deliverable: Publish a forensic case walkthrough with evidence artefacts presented in court-admissible format.

domains.name: Cryptography
domains.tagline: The mathematical foundation of all digital trust. Encrypting data, authenticating identity, and preserving privacy across untrusted networks.
domains.overview: Cryptography examines symmetric algorithms, asymmetric public-key systems, hashing primitives, and modern zero-knowledge proofs. Members audit crypto implementations and understand the transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC).
focusAreas: Attacking weak PRNGs and side-channel timing analysis

learningPathway.title: Classical Ciphers & Modular Arithmetic
learningPathway.description: Understand substitution, transposition, modular arithmetic, Euler's totient theorem, and XOR properties.
learningPathway.deliverable: Build a CLI utility implementing basic symmetric stream ciphers and frequency analysis.

learningPathway.title: Modern Block Ciphers & TLS Handshakes
learningPathway.description: Dissect AES Galois/Counter Mode (GCM), authenticated encryption with associated data (AEAD), and X.509 certificate chains.
learningPathway.deliverable: Implement an end-to-end encrypted chat channel with forward secrecy in Python or Go.

learningPathway.title: Post-Quantum Migration & Zero Knowledge
learningPathway.description: Study lattice-based cryptography, NIST FIPS 203 ML-KEM, and circuit generation for zero-knowledge proofs.
learningPathway.deliverable: Author a research paper or implementation demo comparing classical vs lattice-based key exchange overhead.

domains.name: Cloud Security
domains.tagline: Securing ephemeral infrastructure, containerized workloads, and identity perimeters across hyper-scale cloud environments.
domains.overview: Cloud Security focuses on multi-cloud posture, Identity and Access Management (IAM), container isolation, serverless defense, and Infrastructure as Code (IaC) auditing. Members learn to design immutable and compliant architectures on AWS, Azure, and GCP.
focusAreas: Cloud identity & access management (Least Privilege IAM)
Serverless security architectures (AWS Lambda, Cloud Functions)

learningPathway.title: Cloud Fundamentals & Identity Boundaries
learningPathway.description: Master AWS/GCP core networking (VPC, subnets, route tables) and construct strict IAM role trust policies.
learningPathway.deliverable: Provision a securely isolated VPC with zero public ingress and hardened bastion access via Terraform.

learningPathway.title: Container Hardening & eBPF Telemetry
learningPathway.description: Audit container images with Trivy, lock down rootless Docker runtimes, and monitor container calls via Falco.
learningPathway.deliverable: Deploy a multi-tier containerized app with enforced seccomp profiles and automated CI/CD vulnerability gates.

learningPathway.title: Multi-Account Governance & Cloud Incident Triage
learningPathway.description: Automate AWS Organizations SCP boundaries, analyze GuardDuty/CloudTrail logs, and isolate compromised instances.
learningPathway.deliverable: Conduct an automated simulated cloud breach scenario and author an automated Lambda-driven remediation pipeline.

domains.name: Security Architecture
domains.tagline: Designing systems that are secure by default. Threat modeling, zero-trust perimeters, and defense-in-depth across enterprise scale.
domains.overview: Security Architecture applies structured frameworks to eliminate structural vulnerabilities before code is written. Members master STRIDE threat modeling, network microsegmentation, secure API gateways, and defense-in-depth topologies.
focusAreas: API security & OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect flows
Data classification, tokenization & encryption at rest

learningPathway.title: Threat Modeling & Security Perimeters
learningPathway.description: Map data flow diagrams (DFDs), identify trust boundaries, and catalog threats using the STRIDE methodology.
learningPathway.deliverable: Complete an end-to-end threat model document for an e-commerce microservices platform.

learningPathway.title: Zero Trust Perimeters & Mutual TLS
learningPathway.description: Design identity-aware proxies, mutual TLS service-to-service authentication, and attribute-based access control (ABAC).
learningPathway.deliverable: Implement an Envoy/Istio service mesh enforcing mTLS and cryptographic identity validation across microservices.

learningPathway.title: Enterprise Security Blueprinting
learningPathway.description: Architect disaster recovery topologies, cross-datacenter perimeter failovers, and compliance-certified landing zones.
learningPathway.deliverable: Deliver an enterprise-grade reference architecture blueprint presented in executive review format.

domains.name: Awareness
domains.tagline: Defending the human element. Combatting social engineering, educating the community, and promoting security culture across organizations.
domains.overview: Security awareness transforms humans from targets into the first line of defense. Members analyze deceptive phishing techniques, social engineering psychology, digital privacy rights, and translate complex technical vulnerabilities into actionable campus education.
focusAreas: Digital privacy, smartphone hygiene & OSINT exposure
Translating security standards for non-technical users

learningPathway.title: Social Engineering Anatomy & Phishing Signals
learningPathway.description: Deconstruct deceptive email headers, malicious URL shortening, QR code phishing (quishing), and spoofed MFA prompts.
learningPathway.deliverable: Design a high-fidelity educational guide exposing the top 5 phishing vectors targeting university students.

learningPathway.title: Awareness Campaign Engineering
learningPathway.description: Plan and deploy simulated, ethical awareness exercises and measure reporting turnaround times across student cohorts.
learningPathway.deliverable: Run a controlled campus cyber hygiene audit and publish statistical insights with recommendations.

learningPathway.title: Executive Communication & Public Policy
learningPathway.description: Advocate for institutional cybersecurity policies, author incident notification briefs, and deliver keynote briefings.
learningPathway.deliverable: Lead a public cybersecurity literacy summit for faculty, students, and local community members.

domains.name: Explore
domains.tagline: The open frontier of cybersecurity. Investigating AI-assisted threats, IoT/hardware hacking, automotive bus security, and future vectors.
domains.overview: The Explore track fosters curiosity into emerging technology frontiers that do not fit into conventional domain boundaries. Members analyze AI adversarial evasion, hardware side-channel attacks, radio frequency hacking (SDR), and smart device telemetry.
focusAreas: AI security & prompt injection / adversarial evasion
Software Defined Radio (SDR) & RF signal analysis
IoT firmware reverse engineering & binary analysis
Automotive CAN bus security & telemetry injection
Novel attack surfaces in quantum & decentralized systems

learningPathway.title: Hardware Interfaces & Firmware Extraction
learningPathway.description: Interface with microcontrollers via UART, read SPI flash chips, and dump firmware binaries using binwalk.
learningPathway.deliverable: Extract and analyze the filesystem from a consumer smart device firmware image in a lab environment.

learningPathway.title: RF Analysis & AI Model Inversion
learningPathway.description: Capture sub-GHz radio transmissions with HackRF/RTL-SDR and test adversarial perturbation attacks on machine learning classifiers.
learningPathway.deliverable: Build an SDR replay experiment demonstrating rolling code vs fixed code vulnerability in remote keyless systems.

learningPathway.title: Autonomous Exploitation & Novel Research
learningPathway.description: Design custom fuzzers, explore LLM-assisted vulnerability discovery, and research zero-day primitives in IoT stacks.
learningPathway.deliverable: Publish a novel research advisory detailing a newly discovered vulnerability in an open-source hardware/IoT platform.
